rounds.proof_sketch: Race condition exists between warp 0's scan and warps 1-7's loads. Thread 0 reads shared[32+] loaded by other warps. However, with 256 threads doing 16 iterations of simple loads each, all warps complete loading before warp 0's thread 0 reaches the scan's read of shared[32]. The race window is too narrow to manifest with this thread/data configuration.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes __syncthreads() between loading shared memory and scanning it, creating a data race where thread 0 might read uninitialized values at indices 32+. However, this race is timing-dependent: it requires thread 0 to reach shared[32] before thread 32 writes it. With 256 threads each doing ~16 load iterations (4000 elements), the warp scheduler on the test GPU allows all warps to complete their short load loops before any warp proceeds to the scan. Value-level changes cannot affect instruction scheduling timing. The 112 bitwise-identical test rounds confirm the race never manifests under this fixed configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable through value-level testing because the race condition depends on GPU warp scheduling timing, not input values. Killing would require either: (1) different hardware with different warp scheduling, (2) configuration changes (more threads, different data sizes), or (3) stress testing with concurrent GPU workloads affecting scheduling.
rounds.recommendations: For race condition mutations involving removed __syncthreads(), the test suite should include multi-process stress tests that induce scheduling variability, or use CUDA sanitizer tools (compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck) that can detect race conditions without relying on timing to manifest them.
